docdesigner

Knit attractive, publication-quality documents from R Markdown without deep LaTeX or design knowledge.

docdesigner is a token-driven rendering engine plus distributable style sets. A style is a small YAML file of design tokens; the engine turns those tokens into LaTeX. Styles are self-contained and independently upgradeable, and sets can be installed from GitHub.

Status: 0.11.0, alpha. R CMD check passes on Linux and Windows, all seventeen styles render, and 108 checks that each style’s tokens reach the page pass. See Known limitations. Testers can start with alpha-testing-instructions.pdf, or TESTING.md for the short version.

See every style as a sample PDF in the style gallery.

Install 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("jncohen/docdesigner")

PDF output needs Pandoc 3.1.8 or newer (RStudio includes it) and xelatex (TinyTeX is enough).

Outputs

  • docdesigner::pdf: a designed PDF, set in one of the styles.
  • docdesigner::html: plain body HTML for pasting into WordPress or another CMS.

Minimal YAML 

---
title: "Document Title"
author: "Your Name"
output:
  docdesigner::pdf:
    style: policy
---

PDF options:

---
title: "Document Title"
author:
  - name: "First Author"
    dept: "Department of Sociology"
    inst: "Queens College, CUNY"
    address: "65-30 Kissena Blvd, Queens, NY 11367"
    email: "first.author@example.edu"
    web: "example.edu/~first"
  - name: "Second Author"
warning: "DRAFT IN PROGRESS: DO NOT CIRCULATE"
acknowledgements: |
  I thank the department's workshop for comments.
output:
  docdesigner::pdf:
    style: methods
    title_layout: page
    doublespace: true
---
  • doublespace: true double-spaces the body text, as for a manuscript under review. Titles, headings, tables, captions, footnotes and code stay single-spaced.
  • title_layout: page gives the title, byline and abstract a page of their own; header (the default in every style) sets them at the top of page 1.
  • author is a plain string or a list of people. Each person’s name appears in the byline, with several authors stacked. The corresponding author (marked corresponding: true, otherwise the first author with an address, email or web) gets a contact block: name, dept and inst, address, and linked email and web. orcid is accepted but not printed yet.
  • kicker replaces the small label some styles set above the title (“POLICY BRIEF” in policy, “WORKING PAPER” in ssrn and economist): kicker: "Research Brief". kicker: "" removes it, and any style accepts one.
  • warning is a line such as “DRAFT IN PROGRESS: DO NOT CIRCULATE”, set between two rules. acknowledgements (or acknowledgments) is a paragraph or more of thanks.
  • On a title page the contact block, the warning and the acknowledgements stack at the foot of the page, in that order. In the header layout the warning sits above the title, and the contact details and acknowledgements become an unnumbered note at the foot of page 1.

Warning: tables in two-column styles (nature, economist). A two-column page cannot hold a table that breaks across pages, so in these styles every table becomes a float, placed by LaTeX:

  • A table may not appear where you put it. It moves to the top of a column or page, often after the paragraph that follows it. Refer to tables by number (“Table 2”), never as “the table below”.
  • A table that fits one column stays in the column; a wider one spans both columns and moves to the top of the next page that has room.
  • A table is never split. One taller than a page runs off the bottom. Keep tables short, or split them yourself.
  • Column widths are not kept. Text in cells does not wrap, so a long cell widens the whole table. Keep cell text short.

For long or wide tables, use a single-column style.

---
title: "Article Title"
output:
  docdesigner::html
---

Starters 

docdesigner::designer_use(template = "pdf")       # or "html"

RStudio users can also pick the package templates from File > New File > R Markdown > From Template.

Writing a thesis

Two styles set a thesis: thesis, plain and conservative, and qc-thesis, the same with the Queens College title page for the MA in Data Analytics and Applied Social Research. Both use the thesis title layout: a title page with the degree statement, an optional copyright page, then contents, acknowledgements and abstract numbered i, ii, iii, with chapters starting on new pages from page 1.

---
title: "Thesis Title"
author: "Student Name"
date: "May 2027"
degree: "Master of Arts in Sociology"     # qc-thesis fills this in
institution: "Queens College"             # one line, or a list of lines
committee:
  - name: "Faculty Member"
    role: "Committee Chair"
  - name: "Second Reader"
    role: "Committee Member"
signatures: true      # signature lines on the title page; qc-thesis default
copyright: true       # adds a copyright page
toc: true
acknowledgements: |
  ...
abstract: |
  ...
output:
  docdesigner::pdf:
    style: qc-thesis
---

Each level-one heading (#) is a chapter. signatures: false removes the signature block. Any style can use the thesis layout with title_layout: thesis under docdesigner::pdf:.

Reviewing a draft

The review style is for a manuscript printed to read and mark up by hand. It is not a publication look: every choice serves reading slowly, writing on the page, and finding each mark again in the source.

---
title: "Paper Title"
output:
  docdesigner::pdf:
    style: review
    changes_since: v1.0     # optional: a git tag, commit, or earlier copy
---
  • A 3in right margin on every page, and space between paragraphs, for handwritten insertions. A short ragged measure with no hyphenation.
  • Line numbers (every 5th, restarting on each page) in the right margin and paragraph numbers in the left one, so “p. 7, l. 15” or “para. 14” names a spot in this printout and the next.
  • The body opens with a map of the argument: every heading to two levels, its words and its page. Write headings as claims; a heading of fewer than four words is flagged LABEL? in the margin.
  • The running head names the section’s claim; the foot stamps the title, the git version (+ when the file has uncommitted changes) and the date.
  • [[TODO: words]], [[CITE]], [[WEAK]], [[CUT]], [[CHECK]] and [[FIX]] in the text print as margin tags. Citation keys print after citations.
  • Changebars mark every paragraph changed since the latest git tag, or since changes_since. They compare prose, ignoring inline R code, citations and numbers, so an .Rmd reference works as it is.
  • Nothing floats: tables and figures stay where they are written.

Each feature is a markup.* token, off in every other style, and markup = list(...) turns one off for a single render: docdesigner::pdf(style = "review", markup = list(line_numbers = 0)).

Styles and style sets

A style is a directory containing format.yml. A set is a directory of styles with a set.yml manifest. Seventeen styles ship in two sets:

inst/sets/
  academic/
    set.yml
    styles/
      minimal/ modern/ nature/ methods/ demography/ ssrn/ sociology/ ajs/
      review/ thesis/ qc-thesis/
  public/
    set.yml
    styles/
      policy/ government/ economist/ atlantic/ humanities/ bulletin/
designer_styles()             # every installed style
designer_sets()               # every installed set
designer_style("methods")     # fully resolved tokens for one style
designer_gallery()            # HTML swatch table
designer_specimens()          # render a PDF specimen per style + gallery index

A style file

format.yml is a flat list of dotted-key tokens — one key: value per line. It declares only its identity (id, label, description) and the tokens that differ from the engine defaults; anything omitted falls back to the schema (inst/engine/schema.yml). Run designer_tokens() for the full vocabulary, and see Creating a style for how to write a style and what makes a good one.

id: methods
label: Methods
description: Computational social science and methods journals
inherits: modern             # optional; resolves a full chain

typography.body: "Source Serif 4"
typography.heading: "Source Serif 4"
typography.mono: "Fira Code"
typography.base_size: "10pt"

color.accent: "003DA5"
color.rule: "003DA5"

headings.number_sections: true
headings.h1.scale: 1.30
headings.h1.rule.position: below
headings.h1.rule.weight: medium
headings.h2.scale: 1.12

title.layout: header
title.rule.position: below
title.rule.weight: thick
title.rule.color: rule

code.highlight: tango

Point a document at a style directory to try it without installing:

output:
  docdesigner::pdf:
    style: "path/to/my-style"

Creating a style 

designer_new_style("my-style", from = "minimal", path = "~/styles")

The scaffold contains the source style’s declared tokens only, not the resolved defaults, so it keeps tracking engine changes. Edit, then render a specimen to see it:

designer_specimens(styles = "my-style")

Installing a set from GitHub 

designer_install_set("academic")                   # from the canonical library, jncohen/docdesigner
designer_install_set(repo = "owner/repo")           # a dedicated repo with set.yml at its root
designer_install_set("some-set", repo = "owner/monorepo")  # a set inside someone else's monorepo
designer_update_sets()                              # re-pull recorded sources

Sets install under tools::R_user_dir("docdesigner", "data") and survive package updates. A user set shadows a core style of the same id, with a warning. Sets declare a format_version; the engine refuses to load a set from a newer format rather than mis-render it.

Fonts

Styles and sets may declare their own font families and ship the files alongside. Lookup order is style → set → core:

my-set/
  set.yml
  assets/fonts/Inter-Regular.otf
  assets/fonts/Inter-Bold.otf
  styles/my-style/format.yml
fonts.Inter.regular: Inter-Regular.otf
fonts.Inter.bold: Inter-Bold.otf
typography.body: Inter
typography.heading: Inter

All faces of a family must live in one directory — fontspec’s Path= applies per family.

Checking your setup 

designer_check()

Reports whether the template, fonts, citation style, styles, Pandoc and a LaTeX engine can all be found.

Known limitations

  1. Tables in two-column styles (nature, economist) are floats: they move, never split across pages, and lose their column widths. See the warning above.
  2. The author orcid is not printed.
  3. bulletin uses TeX Gyre Heros, which full TeX installations include. With TinyTeX, add it once: tinytex::tlmgr_install("tex-gyre").
  4. The last page of a two-column document is not balanced, so the right column can end well above the left.
  5. The bundled fonts take 3.4 MB. That is too large for CRAN, which is on hold until they move.

Repository layout 

R/
  engine.R                  token resolution, fonts, dd_preamble(), pdf()
  schema.R                  reads and validates the token schema
  sets.R                    install, list, update and scaffold styles and sets
  specimens.R               designer_specimens()
  html.R  html-assets.R     html() and its image and checklist helpers
  gallery.R  check.R  use.R  styles.R  design_brief.R  import_html.R  utils.R
inst/engine/schema.yml      the token vocabulary and its defaults
inst/engine/*.lua           pandoc filters: authors, tables, table headers,
                            callouts, drop caps
inst/templates/docdesigner.tex   the LaTeX template pdf() renders through
inst/sets/                  the bundled style sets
inst/fonts/                 bundled fonts (3.4 MB)
inst/specimen/specimen.md   the document designer_specimens() renders
inst/rmarkdown/templates/   RStudio starter templates
design-sets/                style drafts; not part of the package
examples/                   example documents, including the gallery specimen
dev/                        development scripts (render, verify, specimens)
pkgdown/assets/specimens/   the gallery's PDFs and thumbnails
tests/test-package.R        tests run by R CMD check; they do not render PDFs
